title: Choose a visual direction for customer sign-in and setup
question: Which direction should shape customer sign-in and organization setup? What should carry forward, what feels false to Showoff, and should the selected concept be approved, combined, revised, or rejected?

options.label: Workspace Docket
options.lineage: A small-business service docket with numbered, carbon-copy steps
options.thesis: Signing in is the first clear step into a customer workspace.
options.viewport: A single setup docket presents Google and Apple sign-in, email and password, and one Continue action without implying an existing organization.
options.risk: The service-form structure can feel procedural if the first step is not welcoming.

raised.raise: Progress stays visible, and session or validation states remain explicit rather than disappearing.

options.label: Utility-Red Account Index
options.thesis: Compact account modules keep sign-in choices and setup steps in one scan.
options.viewport: A clearly separated provider area, email form, and next-step summary share one strict grid.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the structure clarifies provider and password entry; high density may be less comfortable for first-time owners.
options.risk: Small labels can make a sensitive first-use task harder to scan.

options.label: Full-Viewport Media Feed
options.thesis: One full-screen media item leads into the customer journey.
options.case: Fuses poorly: sign-in and organization setup are form tasks, not a media sequence.
options.risk: A background video would distract from account access.
options.kept: Keep the primary account task focused within the viewport.

options.label: Opening-Day Guide Map
options.lineage: A zoo and gardens guide map
options.thesis: A widening map lobe shows the route from sign-in into a workspace.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the map does not clarify credential entry or account recovery.
options.risk: Map controls may be mistaken for navigation rather than setup progress.
options.kept: A progress path should make the next step clear.

options.label: Orienteering Course Map
options.thesis: The account route is a fixed map with a clearly marked next control.
options.case: Fuses poorly: navigation symbolism adds decoding work to authentication.
options.risk: The user has no need to choose a route through sign-in.
options.kept: Show which setup step is current and what follows.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Account creation unfolds as a compact wallet of sequential coupons.
options.case: Fuses poorly: travel paperwork is less recognizable than a work setup form to this audience.
options.risk: Flight cues may make the app feel like a travel service.
options.kept: Keep setup stages in order and show which remain.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Account fields use distinct marks to show validated, pending, or held states.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the specialist darkroom grammar is unfamiliar during basic account setup.
options.risk: Technical notation can raise cognitive load.
options.kept: Use clear non-color cues for errors and validation.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar sign-in screen makes account access direct and predictable.
canonCard.viewport: A compact sign-in panel offers provider buttons, email and password fields, and a create-account link.
canonCard.risk: The form may be difficult to distinguish from other SaaS sign-in pages.
